title: China opens a consultation on exporting large-model technology
friendlyTitle: China asks for comments on new AI export rules
summary: China's commerce ministry said on 16 October that it and the science ministry have opened a public consultation on adding technology to the export-control catalogue, and that exporters must register covered exports until a final revision takes effect. The spokesperson said the AI portion would add 23 areas, including large models, agents, and compute clusters. A proposed ban covers AI tools that generate or alter malicious code. Open-source publication would get automatic licensing, technology already public would stay outside the list, and offering a restricted model by API, app, or website would not count as a technology export. Installing that technology on servers abroad would.
friendlySummary: China's commerce ministry said on 16 October that it wants public comments on adding AI technology to its export list. The proposal covers 23 areas, including large models, agents, and computing clusters. Tools that write malicious code would be banned from export. Open-source releases would get a fast approval. Calling a model through an app or website would not count as exporting the technology. Installing it on servers abroad would.
whyItMatters: If you rely on a Chinese open model, the draft is not a shutdown, and the ministry says work that is already public would be exempt. It does create a switch the government could later use for models and weights that are not yet public, and for companies that want to install restricted systems on foreign servers. The rules are still a consultation, not a finished catalogue.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This is a draft, not a finished law. Models that are already public would stay outside the list. The draft would still let the government control future model weights, and control companies that install restricted systems on foreign servers.
